title: Detective didn't know about Taser
article: The police officers involved in an arrest where a man died after he was zapped by a Taser did not tell the investigating police detective that the device had been used, a coroners inquest heard Wednesday.

Vancouver Det. Sean Trowski said he found out in the hours after Robert Bagnell died as he conducted interviews. "One of the tenants told us. We were still unclear at that point that a Taser had been used," Trowski testified.
And the detective said he couldn't secure the two devices that were used until the following day.
Trowski explained that each Taser has built-in software that records how often it was fired and for how long.

While one Taser verified it was discharged as reported by the officer, the software on the other device malfunctioned. Police say they jolted Bagnell twice while trying to arrest him. A pathologist told the inquiry Tuesday that she counted 13 red, dot-like markings on Bagnell's body but she couldn't confirm the marks were made by a Taser. Each Taser zap leaves two dots from the weapon's two barbs.
The pathologist also said Bagnell had extremely high levels of cocaine and methamphetamine in his system.
Bagnell had had heart surgery in the past and when he died, his heart was one and a half times normal size, Dr. Laural Gray testified. She said he died of a heart attack.
She also said the Taser wasn't responsible for killing Bagnell because Bagnell continued to struggle after getting jolted and if the Taser were responsible, he would have stopped.
Police used the Taser to subdue Bagnell who was on a violent rampage in a hotel washroom in June 2004.
Trowski said a fire on the first floor of the building forced the police to make a decision to attempt an arrest.
"It was an extremely dangerous situation with the age of the building," he said. "It was a significant factor in my opinion."
